title: Risk & Control Manager
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Risk Manager to join our Risk & Control team, part of Pleo's Second Line of Defence. You'll report to our Head of Risk and Control, helping build and run our enterprise risk management framework, from risk appetite linkage through to the risk reporting our senior leaders and committees rely on. Alongside that full ERM remit, you'll own second line oversight of security, technology and operational resilience risk, giving our technology and security teams informed, credible challenge. It's a rare mix: a broad enterprise risk role with a technology risk specialism, in a FinTech that's still shaping how it manages risk as it scales. We value people from a range of risk backgrounds, so if you match most of what's below, we'd love to hear from you. Who you'll be working with and reporting to You'll report to our Head of Risk and Control, who leads Pleo's second line risk function and our enterprise risk management framework. You'll work closely with our Assurance & Controls Manager on testing, our Credit & Product Risk Officer, and the security GRC team in the First Line, as well as teams across Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance and Compliance. What you’ll be doing As a Risk Manager, you will: Build and run our ERM framework: Act as deputy to the Head of Risk and Control on our enterprise risk management framework, including risk appetite, how it links to our risks and controls, and the reporting that goes to senior management and governance committees. Own technology and security risk oversight: Lead 2LOD oversight of information security, technology and operational resilience risk, setting the methodology and standards and challenging the First Line on where the gaps are. Test our IT general controls: Run ITGC testing with our technology and security teams, assessing whether controls are well designed and working in practice. Lead high-risk testing when incidents happen: Partner with our Assurance & Controls Manager to lead incident-driven testing in our highest-risk areas and turn findings into clear actions. Run risk assessments and RCSAs: Lead risk assessments and risk and control self-assessments across the business, not just in technology. Shape our GRC tooling: Run pilots of GRC tools and help decide how we bring more structure and automation to how we manage risk. Be a trusted risk partner: Advise First Line teams on risk, regulatory change and the control environment, and support our engagement with regulators. Right now we're broadening what the team covers. We already have strong financial and credit risk skills in the team. This hire closes our gap in technology risk and gives us a second person who can run enterprise risk management end to end. You'll work across a risk universe that spans technology, information security, privacy and operational resilience, alongside product, operational and financial risk. What you bring You’ll thrive in this role if you have: Enterprise risk management depth: Hands-on experience running an ERM or operational risk framework in a regulated financial services business (FinTech, banking, payments or similar), including risk appetite, risk reporting and RCSAs. You could step in for the Head of Risk and Control when needed. Technology risk know-how: Hands-on experience applying security, technology and operational resilience risk methodology and standards, with enough depth to challenge technology and security teams credibly. You don't need to be an engineer. Controls testing experience: A track record of ITGC testing or similar control testing and assurance work. The ability to influence: Confidence engaging stakeholders on complex or sensitive risk topics, challenging constructively and being heard. Clear, collaborative communication: The ability to translate risk concepts into practical language for everyone from engineers to senior leadership. A pragmatic mindset: A drive to find workable answers to real risk challenges rather than defaulting to theory. Nice to have: First Line experience, for example in an IT, security or GRC team before moving into second line risk Experience with GRC tooling, including selecting or rolling out a platform Exposure to data risk or AI risk Experience at both a FinTech and a traditional bank or payments business How you’ll develop in this role In your first 12 months at Pleo, you’ll: Get under the skin of Pleo's risk landscape and take ownership of key 2LOD review and challenge activities across priority business areas. Play an active role in evolving our risk framework as the company continues to scale — contributing your expertise to initiatives that will shape how we manage risk for years to come. Build strong relationships across the business, establishing yourself as a credible and trusted voice on risk matters. We're committed to helping you grow here, whether that means deepening your technical expertise, expanding your regulatory knowledge, or stepping into broader leadership responsibilities as the team develops. Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You've run enterprise or operational risk frameworks and want to go deeper on technology and security risk You started in IT, security or technology risk and have since moved into broad, enterprise-wide risk management You enjoy building and improving frameworks in a scaling business, and want to be a genuine deputy to the head of the function This role is not a good fit for you if: Your experience is mainly First Line security or GRC work without broad enterprise risk management. This role covers the whole risk universe, not just technology Your background is primarily consultancy, internal audit or compliance without substantial hands-on risk and control experience You want a mature, settled framework to maintain. A lot of this role is building, testing and piloting while the business moves around you How you'll develop in this role In your first 12 months at Pleo, you'll: Take ownership of key ERM framework deliverables alongside the Head of Risk and Control, including risk appetite linkage and committee reporting Set our technology and operational resilience risk methodology and complete a full cycle of ITGC testing Run a GRC tooling pilot through to a clear recommendation on how we manage risk at scale As deputy to the head of the function, you'll get broad exposure to senior stakeholders and governance, with room to grow into wider leadership as the team develops. The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Hiring manager interview: A conversation with our Head of Risk and Control. Peer interview: A conversation with two members of our Risk & Control team. Final interview: A conversation with our Chief Risk Officer. Show me the benefits! Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis We offer 25+ days of holiday + your public holidays For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we're looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired a Risk Manager, we received a lot of applications but only meet with a select few. With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application: We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it's a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the "Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z" formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you've worked on. title: Senior Data Product Partner - (Spend & Control)
description: About Us Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact. We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem . Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work. At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team. Visit www.perk.com to learn more. The Opportunity: We are building a new team of Data Product Partners to bridge the gap between business needs and complex data systems, ensuring our data assets are trustworthy, discoverable, impactful and truly solve user problems. As a Senior Data Product Partner (DPP) , you will be the driving force behind the impact of our data team with the Perk business. You will move fluently between business and data worlds, making critical decisions rooted in both user needs and technical reality. Your goal is to move beyond simply providing solutions to proving demonstrable business impact. Role Title: Senior Data Product Partner Reporting To: Manager, Data Product Partner Core Mandate: Be the primary data consultant, fixer, strategist, and relationship manager for a specific business domain (e.g. Customer Care, Finance, Marketing, Revenue, Spend & Control, Travel) We are open to either Regular or Senior profiles What You’ll Do: Relationship Management and Strategy Develop Business Data Strategy: Collaborate with business leaders to define how data can drive their strategic goals, solve critical challenges, and uncover new opportunities Identify and Qualify Value: Proactively identify high-impact use cases and data initiatives that will generate maximum measurable value (e.g., revenue increase, cost reduction, efficiency gain) for the partner business unit Act as the primary translator across all disciplines, explaining the same concept differently to different data team roles and executives Proactively manage expectations and define the appropriate scope and flexible roadmaps Develop Product Sense for Data, anticipating common data quality issues, recognising when simpler solutions are better, and strategically saying "no" to requests that compromise our aligned vision Publicise and amplify the work that has been done to drive adoption of and learning from our solutions Coach teams to be able to self serve their own preliminary investigations Demand Shaping and Portfolio Management Focus on defining what to build and why (Data Product Partner) rather than how (AE/ DA/ DE/ DS/ DG). Ensuring that we built the right thing - vs the Data Team Lead owning did we build the thing right While the Data teams own the timeline estimates, the DPP defines the urgency, the required business target date and the prioritisation, which then influences how the Craft team approaches the estimate Shape and Prioritise Demand: Work with business stakeholders to clarify their data needs, translating vague requests into well-defined, measurable projects and technical data requirements that can be handed over to the Data Teams Manage the Business Unit's Data Portfolio: Oversee the pipeline of data projects, data products and initiatives relevant to their business unit, ensuring alignment with capacity and strategic priorities. Work closely with Data teams to evaluate technical tradeoffs with potential business impact Conduct Value Realisation Tracking: Continuously monitor and report on the actual business outcomes and ROI delivered by completed data projects and products Ad-Hoc Analysis, Triage & Intake Management The Data Product Partner is the first line of response for data questions from the business and plays a critical role in determining the right level of effort and ownership Conduct initial ad-hoc analysis where appropriate, including lightweight SQL queries, exploratory analysis in Looker as well as quick validations, sanity checks, and hypothesis testing Use this initial analysis to answer simple, time-sensitive business questions directly, clarify the underlying problem and assess feasibility, data quality, and potential impact Triage and prioritise ad-hoc requests by determining whether the request can be resolved quickly vs. requires deeper analytical or engineering work. Escalate and hand over well-defined requests to Data Analytics, Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Science or Data Governance when needed. Provide clear context, urgency, and success criteria to downstream teams Actively identify recurring ad-hoc requests that indicate a gap in existing dashboards or data products, a need for improved data quality, documentation, or enablement or an opportunity to convert reactive work into scalable data products Consultation and Enablement Provide Data Consulting: Offer expert advice to business stakeholders on data availability, appropriate methodologies, and the interpretation of data insights Drive Data Literacy and Adoption: Champion the use of data tools and insights within the business unit, coaching teams on how to effectively integrate data into their daily decision-making processes Proactively surface observations, trends, or risks as nuggets of insight Bridge the Data-to-Action Gap: Ensure that insights are clearly communicated, translated and embedded into concrete business actions and process changes Ensure that the pain points of Data Quality gaps are identified and prioritised within the Data Team AI at Perk AI is embedded in how we work across every function. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes. How We Work At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. Mission. Action. Growth. Inclusion. Care.</p> <p>It's at the heart of everything we do. Within our People Collective, we're here to bring brilliant people together, build an inclusive culture and create an environment where everyone can do their best work. As Monzo continues to grow, our offices play an important role in bringing our people together. They're more than just places to work. You'll lead a team of six across four office locations in London, Cardiff, Dublin and Barcelona, helping us deliver an exceptional workplace experience while managing and developing our global property portfolio.</p> <p>Reporting to the Head of Property, Culture and Engagement, you'll oversee our daily operations, lead strategic projects and collaborate with teams across Monzo to create safe, welcoming and engaging workplaces that bring people together and put the Monzonaut community first.</p> <h2><strong>🔑 You'll play a key role by...</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>🏢 Leading our global property and facilities operations</strong> – Overseeing our office locations, ensuring they're safe and compliant, while delivering a consistent and delightful workplace experience.</li> <li><strong>🚀 Managing and delivering property projects</strong> – Leading projects from planning to delivery, including office moves, refurbishments and new site launches. You'll manage timelines, budgets and internal and external stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.</li> <li><strong>🌍 Supporting our global property strategy</strong> – Turning our longer term property ambitions into practical plans, ensuring our spaces meet the needs of our people and support Monzo's continued growth.</li> <li><strong>💪 Leading and developing a brilliant team</strong> – Managing six team members across all locations, setting clear priorities, supporting their development and building a scalable, high-performing function.</li> <li><strong>🤝 Collaborating across Monzo</strong> – Building strong relationships with Finance, Legal, TechOps and senior leadership to align priorities, influence decisions and deliver improvements.</li> <li><strong>💰 Managing budgets and suppliers</strong> – Overseeing property and facilities budgets, managing supplier relationships and ensuring we're delivering value for money across our portfolio.</li> <li><strong>🦺 Keeping our spaces safe and sustainable</strong> – Ensuring our workplaces meet health and safety requirements, managing compliance and working with the ESG team to deliver our Scope 1 and 2 environmental commitments.</li> <li><strong>✨ Continuously improving how we work</strong> – Using data and employee feedback to improve our spaces, streamline processes and build scalable ways of working. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. title: Senior Customer Success Manager
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><a href="https://fin.ai/">Fin</a>, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.</p> <p>Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.</p> <p>Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.</p> <p>Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.</p></div><h2><strong>What's the opportunity? </strong> </h2> <p>As a Strategic CSM, you’ll partner with our largest and most complex customers to help them succeed in the new era of AI-driven customer service. You’ll work with C-suite leaders and their Support teams to guide them through their AI Agent transformation with Fin — from early project scoping and requirements gathering, to measurable adoption, to industry-best automation rates and business outcomes. </p> <p>This role is an opportunity to shape how the world’s leading companies deploy AI to transform their support operations and achieve strategic outcomes aligned to their business goals.</p> <h2><strong>Responsibilities</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Develop trusted advisor relationships with customers (from c-suite stakeholders to individual contributors).</li> <li>Facilitate requirements gathering and process mapping for standard operating procedures; document in clear, precise, and actionable terms.</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers to translate customer requirements into Fin solution designs, guiding the customer on configuration best practices and prompt strategy.</li> <li>Monitor Fin usage patterns to identify risks, recommend optimizations, and uncover expansion opportunities. </li> <li>Maintain deep product knowledge of Fin’s fast-expanding capabilities; remain market aware of the fast evolving AI-agent industry.</li> <li>Lead Success Plans, QBRs/EBRs, and strategic planning sessions with the customer.</li> <li>Prioritize competing demands to drive the highest-value outcomes across your customer portfolio.</li> <li>Be the Voice of the Customer internally, advocating for customers’ needs and shaping our solutions strategy.</li> </ul> <h2>What skills do I need? </h2> <ul> <li>8+ years of customer-facing experience in management consulting, strategy, advisory, or enterprise SaaS CSM roles.</li> <li>Experience with business process mapping, requirements analysis, and solution design.</li> <li>Strong technical acumen and passion for AI/agent-building (coding not required).</li> <li>Ability to simplify and communicate complex problems clearly across audiences.</li> <li>Strong prioritization skills to effectively manage a broad portfolio of customer accounts while delivering depth of impact.</li> <li>Demonstrated success driving adoption, process improvement, and measurable outcomes for enterprise customers.</li> <li>Self-motivated, adaptable, and curious team player with a high level of self-efficacy</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Unleash Your Potential</strong></p> <p>When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.</p> <p>In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Offerings vary by location in line with local practices and requirements. Learn more about working at Fin and the benefits we offer at<a href="http://fin.ai/careers"> fin.ai/careers</a>. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Salesforce will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. </p> <p><strong>Policies </strong></p> <p>Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.</p> <p>We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. description: About Us Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. About the Role The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an Engagement Manager to join our UK & Ireland Engagement team in London, own adoption across a portfolio of enterprise corporate clients and help some of the world's largest in-house legal functions fundamentally change the way they work. This is a role for someone who has led change inside large, complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed. You will own the adoption and long-term success of strategic enterprise accounts: building deep, multi-level relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser who turns Legora into an embedded part of how those teams operate. Enterprise means depth: larger, more complex accounts with more revenue at stake. Each account is a global legal function with multiple teams, jurisdictions and business units, its own governance, and a long, multi-phase roadmap. Success depends on navigating that complexity: aligning General Counsel, legal operations, IT, security and procurement, and building momentum one team and one use case at a time until Legora is used across the whole function. At the heart of the role is designing each client's enterprise adoption strategy and delivering the change programmes that transform how they work. For every account you will build a tailored, multi-year roadmap, sequence initiatives from the first pilot teams to function-wide and global adoption, define measurable outcomes and ROI with executive sponsors, and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge. You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class enterprise adoption programme at Legora, helping clients realise measurable ROI, expand successful use cases and transform the way their teams work. What You'll Do You'll lead the post-sale customer experience, owning onboarding, adoption and long-term value realisation for a portfolio of enterprise accounts. Specifically, you will: Design each client's enterprise adoption strategy: the change-management approach, governance model, stakeholder map across legal, business and IT, and target outcomes for how that legal function adopts Legora. Execute against that strategy, sequencing initiatives from the first pilot teams through to function-wide and global adoption across regions, practice areas and business units. Build and run executive governance with each client, including steering committees, executive business reviews and success plans owned jointly with GC and legal operations leadership. Act as a strategic adviser who deeply understands enterprise in-house legal priorities (cost, cycle time, risk, global consistency and doing more without adding headcount), surfaces high-impact opportunities and guides teams towards maximum value from Legora. Navigate the enterprise landscape, including security reviews, IT and integration requirements, procurement and change-control processes, so that adoption keeps moving. Orchestrate engagement from cross-functional teams to accelerate client success (GTM, Product, Legal Engineering, Engineering, Marketing, Support), keeping full account context and coordination. Partner closely with GTM on renewals, expansion and other key commercial moments, building the case for wider deployment and new use cases across the client's organisation. Turn customer feedback into action by working closely with Product, Engineering and Marketing to shape the roadmap, positioning and enablement for enterprise clients. Build reusable enterprise playbooks, governance templates and enablement material from what works, so the whole Engagement team gets better as you go. What You Bring You care deeply about customer outcomes and you know that transformation has to be designed and led. You're proactive, strategic and comfortable steering demanding, senior stakeholders through significant change. You take pride in being the reason customers adopt, grow and succeed. We're looking for: At least 5 years' experience in management consulting, legal, LegalTech or customer success, ideally with enterprise clients in an AI-native B2B vertical. Experience leading large-scale rollouts and adoption programmes at enterprise or global organisations. We want someone who has taken a new way of working into a large, multi-jurisdictional in-house function, navigated procurement, IT, security and sceptical stakeholders, and made it stick. A consulting or transformation background, with a track record of designing and delivering change-management programmes inside large, matrixed organisations. Experience building multi-year, client-level transformation roadmaps and governance structures, and steering them to measurable outcomes. Confidence engaging C-suite and General Counsel-level stakeholders, running executive reviews and building executive sponsorship. Strong programme management: comfortable running complex, multi-workstream programmes with many stakeholders, dependencies and risks. A track record of driving adoption, retention, expansion and satisfaction with enterprise clients. Experience in legal, compliance or other regulated and complex industries, or the ability to learn a complex domain exceptionally fast. Excellent communication skills, written, verbal and interpersonal. You can hold the room with a General Counsel and roll up your sleeves with the teams who use the product every day. High EQ: you know when to listen, when to advise and when to act. A love of fast-paced, early-stage environments where you help build the playbook, not just follow it. Fluency with metrics, and a focus on data, customer health and outcomes over process. title: Senior Data Scientist
description: <p><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/bY0nNPT75xY" width="560" height="314"></iframe></p> <p><strong>Senior Data Scientist | Autoplanner | Hybrid Working | London</strong></p> <p><strong>Introduction:</strong> </p> <p>We are Ocado Group, and we're bringing world-class automation to online grocery. Our Ocado Smart Platform (OSP) combines cutting-edge robotics, AI, and IoT within our advanced CFCs (Customer Fulfilment Centres). We've mastered the single pick, transforming online delivery for our global partners. Join us and be part of a team pushing the boundaries of retail technology.</p> <p><strong>About the Role:</strong></p> <p>As a Senior Data Scientist within our Autoplanner team, you will build AI-powered systems that unify planning across global warehouses and last-mile operations. You will be responsible for developing the machine learning models, optimisation algorithms, and operational simulations that underpin our core planning products. By taking high-impact models from concept through to monitored production systems, you will ensure automated operational plans are robust, globally optimised, and trusted to run live across our partners' international supply chains.</p> <p>Working closely with cross-functional software engineers and product managers, you will set the technical direction for key initiatives while mentoring colleagues to elevate the team’s overall data science capabilities. You will also engage directly with internal and external stakeholders, including global retail partners - to translate complex logistics challenges into production-ready data science solutions, shaping the future of autonomous operational planning.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Deliver machine learning models for planning products, iterating from initial prototype to evaluated and monitored production artefacts.</li> <li>Explore innovative modelling and optimisation approaches, benchmarking and testing them rigorously against existing solutions.</li> <li>Build and extend simulations of warehouse operations and customer demand to validate and power live operational plans.</li> <li>Define and measure business-critical metrics using robust statistical techniques, establishing the team's standards for model evaluation.</li> <li>Set the technical direction and delivery strategy for the data science initiatives you lead.</li> <li>Develop the technical capabilities of data scientists across the team through mentoring, technical guidance, and collaboration.</li> <li>Partner with software engineers to ensure models are cleanly packaged, deployed, monitored, and efficiently served on the platform.</li> <li>Own relationships with product managers, internal partner teams, and external retailers to align on requirements and delivery roadmaps.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We’re Looking For: </strong><em>Essential</em></p> <ul> <li>Proven track record of taking data science and machine learning models into production, maintaining them, and leading initiatives end-to-end.</li> <li>Strong machine learning and statistical expertise, including the ability to evaluate model performance rigorously against business metrics.</li> <li>Fluency in writing production-quality Python code.</li> <li>Experience querying and working with large datasets in cloud data warehouses such as BigQuery, including implementing data-quality checks.</li> <li>Experience building simulations or stochastic models of operational systems.</li> <li>Practical experience using AI coding agents, alongside the critical judgement to verify and test generated code and outputs.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with software engineers, product managers, and diverse business stakeholders.</li> </ul> <p><em>Nice to Haves</em></p> <ul> <li>Experience with mathematical optimisation frameworks and toolkits, such as OR-Tools.</li> <li>Experience with discrete-event simulation libraries, such as SimPy.</li> <li>Background or domain knowledge in logistics, supply chain, or operational research.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Benefits</strong> </p> <p>We believe in supporting our people with meaningful, flexible benefits that prioritise well-being and work-life balance. Here’s a snapshot of what you can expect:</p> <ul> <li>Time to recharge: 25 days annual leave (rising to 27 after 5 years), plus the option to buy more – and 30 days a year to work from anywhere in the world.</li> <li>Health & wellbeing: Private Medical Insurance from your first month, wellbeing support through specialist apps and EAP, plus Income Protection and Life Assurance.</li> <li>Family-first policies: 22 weeks paid maternity/primary carer leave and 6 weeks paid paternity leave</li> <li>Financial support: Pension with employer matching up to 7%, share schemes (Sharesave & BAYE), and interest-free loans for train tickets.</li> <li>Commuter perks: Cycle to Work Scheme and free shuttle buses to/from Hatfield and Welwyn Garden City stations.</li> <li>Exclusive discounts: 15% off at Ocado.com with free delivery (starting in your first month).</li> </ul> <p>Be bold, be unique, be brilliant, be you. We are looking for individuality and we value diversity. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to treating all applicants and employees fairly and equally. We are committed to making reasonable adjustments to provide a positive, barrier-free recruitment process and supportive work environment. If you have any support or access requirements, we encourage you to advise us at the time of application.</p> <p>#LI-HYBRID</p> <p>#LI-JT1</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Hardware Engineer, FPGA
description: Normal Computing | Build with Us Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London. The Role Validating conventional silicon is a solved discipline. Validating silicon that computes with noise is not, and you will be the one who figures out how. As our FPGA Design Engineer, you will own the bridge between RTL and physical silicon: bringing our physics-inspired ASIC designs to life on FPGA platforms for pre-silicon validation and early software development, and building the test infrastructure for post-silicon bring-up and characterization. Your scope spans the entire FPGA lifecycle: selecting hardware platforms, implementing complex RTL, debugging in the lab, and writing the software that drives it all, working daily with our silicon, EDA, and research teams. What You Will Own FPGA Platform Ownership : Lead the selection, procurement, and bring-up of FPGA prototyping platforms (e.g., HAPS, VCU118/VPK180-class boards, or custom hardware) for pre-silicon RTL validation and software development. RTL Implementation : Adapt and implement complex ASIC RTL onto FPGA targets, including multi-clock-domain architectures, CDC bridges, and timing closure on dense designs. IP Integration : Integrate in-house designs with third-party and vendor IP; serve as the expert on the AMD/Xilinx ecosystem (Vivado IP Integrator, transceivers, memory controllers). High-Speed Interfaces : Design, implement, and validate high-speed I/O with a focus on PCIe: our accelerators ship as PCIe cards in standard servers. Post-Silicon Validation : Build FPGA-based "tester" designs for silicon bring-up, device characterization, and automated test environments. Hardware-Software Stack : Develop the software layer around the hardware: Python/C++ hardware abstraction, register-map generation, and automated build and regression flows. Lab Debug : Root-cause complex timing and functional issues in real time using ILA/Vivado Analyzer, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and BER/eye-diagram characterization of high-speed links. What Makes You a Great Fit Proven industry experience taking FPGA designs from RTL through timing closure to validated hardware, ideally in an ASIC prototyping, emulation, or high-growth hardware environment. Expert-level SystemVerilog and/or VHDL for synthesis, with deep proficiency in Xilinx Vivado (synthesis, place & route, timing closure, IP catalog). Hands-on experience implementing and debugging PCIe, plus AXI/AHB, SPI, UART, JTAG, and other common interfaces. Strong Python for automation, test, and build tooling. Strong board-level bring-up and lab debugging skills on real hardware. Startup mindset: you work independently, pivot quickly, and run at ambiguous problems that span hardware, software, and physics. Bonus Points Verification frameworks like Cocotb or UVM Experience deploying ML models to FPGAs (hls4ml, FINN, or custom NN-to-RTL flows), or building real-time, sub-microsecond signal processing pipelines. Mixed-signal ASIC exposure: digital front-ends, ADC/DAC interfaces, or analog compute. SERDES tuning and signal integrity fundamentals. CI/CD for hardware (GitLab CI, Docker-based build and test). title: Staff Product Engineer
description: About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. How we work We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder , and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work. We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods , usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart. We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move. Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest. A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer. The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 4 , that looks like this: What you'll be doing Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion. Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced. Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve. Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting. Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you. Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating. What you'll need to have done Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered. Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve. Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps. Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to. Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce. Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity. Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them. At Level 4 we'll also look for Set technical direction on a hard problem other engineers built on, and been judged on whether you made them faster and safer rather than on the size of your team. Held a quality bar across other people's work without becoming the gate they wait on. Led cross-cutting or decoupling work that teams adopted because it was the best path, not because it was mandated. You’re unlikely to thrive here if You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach. You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges. You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview process Initial chat with our Talent team Lead Hirer Interview Live AI Skills Assessment Values Interview with the CPTO Meet the CEO Our commitment to Diversity hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team. title: Head of Technical Support
description: 📍 London (Hybrid — 2 days onsite) 🕒 Permanent | Start ASAP We’re Making Travel Effortless. Join Us. Travel is essential, whether it’s visiting family, starting a new adventure, or taking a career defining trip. Yet today, over 4 billion airline passengers rely on tech that hasn't changed in decades. At Duffel, we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underpinning the global travel industry. Backed by top-tier investors (Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures) and born out of Y Combinator (S18), we’re simplifying complex systems to build the future of travel About the role As Head of Technical Support, you’ll lead our team of Technical Support Engineers and take responsibility for the quality, effectiveness and development of the function. You’ll build a team that combines strong technical investigation with clear, thoughtful customer communication. You’ll coach engineers, establish effective ways of working and ensure customers receive dependable support as their integrations grow in complexity and scale. You’ll stay close to the work: reviewing investigations, helping with significant escalations and understanding where our products or processes create friction. Your impact will come from strengthening the whole team’s ability to resolve problems and turning what we learn from support into lasting improvements. You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Partner Engineering, Partner Management and Travel Operations. Technical Support owns day-to-day API questions, troubleshooting and the customer support response to technical incidents. Partner Engineers own strategic technical relationships and solution architecture; Implementation Managers own implementation programmes. What you’ll do Lead and develop the team. Set clear expectations, provide regular coaching and feedback, support career development and address performance issues constructively. Hire and onboard engineers as the team grows. Own support quality. Establish standards for technical investigation, written communication, case ownership and follow-through. Ensure customers understand what is happening, what comes next and who is responsible. Build a dependable support operation. Improve triage, prioritisation, queue management, handovers and escalation paths. Plan staffing and coverage around customer needs and agreed service commitments, with a sustainable workload for the team. Strengthen technical capability. Help engineers investigate API behaviour, interpret logs and request traces, reproduce integration issues and distinguish customer configuration problems from platform or supplier issues. Lead significant customer escalations. Coordinate the support response, establish customer impact and keep communication clear through to resolution. Work with Engineering on diagnosis and recovery, involving Partner Engineering where an issue creates a wider strategic risk. Make collaboration effective. Give Engineering actionable escalation reports with evidence, reproduction steps and impact. Work with Travel Operations on booking and supplier issues, and with implementation teams to ensure new integrations enter support with the context the team needs. Improve the product through support. Identify recurring problems and turn them into clear recommendations for Product and Engineering. Track whether fixes, documentation and product changes actually reduce customer friction. Make support easier to deliver. Develop troubleshooting guides, internal knowledge, customer documentation and useful tooling. Apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, speed and access to help. Use evidence to guide decisions. Monitor response and resolution performance, ageing work, reopened cases, customer feedback and team capacity. Use that information to prioritise improvements and make clear recommendations about investment. What we’re looking for Experience managing and developing a technical support or support engineering team serving business customers. A track record of improving both customer outcomes and how a support function operates. Strong technical understanding of APIs, HTTP, authentication, webhooks and integrations, with enough practical depth to guide investigations and earn the trust of engineers. Comfort working with logs, SQL and scripts to investigate problems or improve support workflows. Experience handling consequential customer escalations, including situations where the cause or resolution is initially uncertain. Ability to explain technical issues to developers, business stakeholders and senior leaders. Sound judgement about urgency, customer impact and competing priorities. Evidence of effective hiring, coaching, performance management and delegation. The ability to influence Product, Engineering and commercial teams through clear reasoning and useful evidence. Comfort building and improving a function in a growing company, while remaining involved in its day-to-day work. Experience that would be useful Supporting an API platform, developer product or infrastructure business. Working with enterprise customers running important production integrations. Leading support across different time zones. Improving support tooling, knowledge management, self-service or automation. Experience in travel technology, payments or another industry with complex external dependencies. You don’t need to have worked in travel or held this exact title. We’re interested in the teams you’ve developed, the problems you’ve solved and the judgement you bring. What success looks like During your first six months: Engineers have clear expectations, regular coaching and practical development plans. Customer issues have clear ownership, appropriate prioritisation and dependable communication. You have established a trustworthy baseline for support performance and delivered measurable improvements in the most important areas. Escalations reach the right teams with better evidence and fewer unnecessary handovers. Recurring problems are being addressed through product changes, documentation or tooling. Duffel has a clear plan for the support capacity and capabilities needed as the business grows. Why You’ll Love Working at Duffel We believe in true ownership. That’s why every permanent employee gets equity in the business. Perks That Actually Matter: ✈️ Travel Allowance: We literally pay you to get out of town and explore the world. 🏝️ Work From Anywhere: Flexibility is built in. Work remotely, or take advantage of our Sabbatical Policy . ⚡ Electric Car Scheme: Roll up in a brand-new EV with eco-friendly tax savings. ⚖️ Work-Life Harmony: Flexible bank holidays, generous family leave, and a dedicated volunteering day. 📚 Growth Tools: Paid study days to level up your skills, plus a solid pension and cycle-to-work scheme. 🏥 Health & Wellbeing: Private healthcare, eye test cover, and season ticket loans. 🏡 Family Leave (maternity, paternity and adoption): Big support for life’s biggest moments, 26 weeks fully paid. The Details 📍 Location: Shoreditch, London (Hybrid: In-office Tuesdays & Thursdays). 🧠 Interview Process: Simple & transparent: (change accordingly to role) Recruiter Screen Hiring Manager Chat Technical Case Study Final Stage Interview. We are an equal opportunities employer. We believe that the key to our success is employing a diverse team, that's why recruitment decisions are only based on your experience and skills. We value your ability to problem solve and build amazing things so we welcome applications for everyone - regardless of age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief. Note to recruitment agencies Duffel does not accept speculative CV's from external parties. Any unsolicited CV's sent to us will be treated as property of Duffel, and any attached terms and conditions associated with these CV's will be null and void. title: Senior / Staff Product Manager
description: V7 At V7, we’re building AI platforms that help humans do their best work, at incredible scale and speed. Our mission is to turn human knowledge into trustworthy AI, making complex tasks faster, smarter, and more accurate. We’re growing fast, backed by leading investors and AI pioneers (including the minds behind Transformers and Gemini). The product V7 Go helps teams turn complex, repeatable work into AI workflows they can run, review and improve . Built for private markets, insurance and real estate, it supports investment diligence, underwriting, claims review and portfolio reporting—from analysing documents and data to generating deliverables and updating connected systems. Your experts define how the work should be done. V7 combines reusable Skills, shared company knowledge and configurable workflows, with citations, audit logs and human review to help teams verify results and control key decisions. It supports models including GPT, Claude and Gemini. Build workflows around your processes. Configure each stage, choose models and tools, and set review steps where human judgement matters. Teams can inspect sources, correct outputs and refine workflows over time. Explore workflows . Give every workflow your firm’s knowledge. The Context Graph connects documents, entities, relationships and source evidence, creating institutional memory that teams and agents can draw on. Turn analysis into work your team can use. Generate editable memos, reports, presentations and spreadsheets, and connect workflows to the tools your business already uses. Explore document generation . Have a look at what we’re building for finance and insurance . The team you’ll be joining and the impact you’ll have You’ll own V7 Go. That’s the whole product, not a corner of it, working with engineers, designers and with the founders close by. Go 4x-ed revenue last year with 160%+ upsell, and we’re running tens of millions of documents through it for customers in finance, insurance and real estate. What you choose to build next is what decides where that goes. The product does a lot of different things for a lot of different teams. A big part of the job is having a view on what it should be, and being willing to say no to the rest. It’s a small product team, so there’s not much process to hide behind. If something’s broken or missing, it’s yours to sort out. What you’ll be doing from day one Owning the roadmap. Deciding what gets built, killing the stuff that doesn’t matter, and shipping continuously rather than in quarterly chunks. Working out which problems are actually worth solving. Sales wants one thing, the loudest customer wants another, and the interesting bet is usually neither. Defining what good looks like before anything gets built, then checking afterwards whether it landed. Adoption, not shipped tickets. Making the trade-off calls. What’s in, what’s out, what’s deliberately a bit rubbish for now, and being able to explain why to whoever asks. Writing things down clearly. Decisions, trade-offs, why we said no to something. It’s how a small team stays pointed the same way. Keeping the whole thing coherent. Workflows, Context Graph and chat need to feel like one product rather than three that happen to share a login. Most of the features are self-serve, so if it needs explaining, that's a product problem. Who you are You’ve owned a product properly, at a startup or somewhere with a serious product culture. Not running a backlog someone else set. You've owned a real product area end to end at a startup or a company with a serious product culture. Discovery through launch, not backlog management. You've built for expert users who know their domain better than you do. B2B SaaS, fintech, insurtech, developer tools, data platforms. You're genuinely hands-on with LLMs and agents. You build with them, you have views on what they're good and bad at, and you can tell a demo from a product. You can hold a conversation with engineers about trade-offs without needing everything translated. You’re happy without much certainty. Priorities move here more than they would somewhere bigger. Opinionated but not precious about it. V7 champions equality and inclusion because diverse teams build better products. Don't check every box? Apply anyway — we value what makes you unique and will support you through the process, just let our Talent team know how they can help. Compensation: £100K – £140K • Offers Equity • £100K – £140K • Offers Equity Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Brand Proposition Lead
description: About us At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels. Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet. We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel. Introducing the Trainline Brand Proposition Team 👋 Reporting into the Head of Brand Proposition, the Brand Proposition Lead will be responsible for the exploration and development of Trainline's consumer proposition across all markets, ensuring it is delivered successfully and in line with insight and research. This role will have a particular focus on our New Business area, where Trainline is exploring new product verticals and entering new markets, giving you true end to end ownership of shaping a proposition from early insight all the way through to launch. You'll work closely with teams across the business, including UX Research, Data Science and Brand Insights early on, and Product, UX, Engineering, Country Managers and Creative Studio as propositions move towards execution. This is a highly cross-functional role, and part of what makes it exciting is connecting the dots between different projects so they build into one coherent brand story. In this role as the Brand Proposition Lead, you will...🚄 Take an insight and data led approach to proposition development, synthesising input from UX Research, Data Science and Brand Insight to build a clear picture of our customer segments Lead the briefing of new research and insight, working closely with the Head of Brand Insights, and keep a close eye on the external market and competitor landscape to spot opportunities Apply behavioural science thinking to shape and test hypotheses that sharpen our propositions Be the voice of the brand and the customer within the New Business area, where Trainline aims to enter new product verticals and disrupt new markets, informing how we best define, communicate and launch new propositions in line with our wider consumer offering and comms platforms Partner with Country Managers and local specialist teams to understand market and customer challenges and shape competitive, compelling solutions Work closely with Product, UX and Engineering to develop and test propositions, helping prioritise the roadmap against business goals and customer needs Collaborate with Senior Brand Managers, Creative Studio and Growth teams to set guidelines for how propositions are executed in market, communicating clearly to build buy-in across the organisation Define success metrics for each proposition, track its product and marketing impact, and report results back to senior stakeholders We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍 Experience working in a tech and/or consumer-oriented industry, comfortable with a fast-paced business A track record of leading projects end to end and getting the right stakeholders involved to keep things moving A curious, analytical mindset, with confidence developing hypotheses, briefing research and using data and insight to guide decisions Comfort managing and communicating with senior stakeholders, including Execs Naturally organised, with experience managing multiple propositions from development through to delivery Strong familiarity with both brand and business performance KPIs Experience working within or alongside product marketing teams It's helpful if you have exposure to AI tools and/or have experience across international European markets, though none of these are dealbreakers More information: Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy. Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated. title: Product Analyst
description: London/Hybrid £40,000 - £60,000 + share options up to £14,500 + Benefits 💬 Accurx is where conversations happen with and about patients. For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. We work alongside our first line credit teams who design the products, decide who to lend to, set underwriting policy, identify customers who need help, manage the portfolio and report and measure credit risk.</p> <p>Within CIF, we are scaling up our Forecasting modelling and execution team to support the enhancement of modelling standards across Finance. The role holder will have the opportunity to lead a ‘consultancy style’ centre of excellence providing thought leadership on the methodological design and regulatory compliance assessment on all Financial forecasting models that feed the banks’ budgeting and stress-testing activities. This will expand to hands-on delivery of model developments, where appropriate. </p> <p>Strong data and analytical skills are a must, as is experience in financial modelling and coding (Python and SQL preferred). Experience working in regulatory stress testing exercises (such as ICAAP or EBA Stress-testing) is highly desirable but not essential. </p> <p>We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies (note we do not expect applicants to have prior experience of all them):</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/">Google Cloud Platform</a> for all of our analytics infrastructure</li> <li><a href="https://www.getdbt.com/">dbt</a> and<a href="https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/"><strong> </strong>BigQuery SQL</a> for our data modelling and warehousing</li> <li>Python for data science and predictive modelling and data visualisation (via streamlit)</li> <li>Anaplan for model implementation</li> <li>Github for version control</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by...</strong></p> <ul> <li>Assisting with continuous improvement of forecasting models via individual delivery or through others</li> <li>Development of best practices for financial modelling across Monzo</li> <li>Presenting forecast model results to senior management</li> <li>Close collaboration with portfolio strategy, model validation, finance and external audit teams</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have a background in financial forecast modelling or execution</li> <li>You have strong analytical skills and a track record of using these to deliver technical projects</li> <li>You have a solid technical toolkit. SQL and Python are our desired coding languages but experience in SAS/R will be considered. A data visualisation tool (such as Streamlit or Looker) is a plus</li> <li>You can convey problems and solutions using clear and simple language, both written and verbal (see <a href="https://monzo.com/tone-of-voice/">Monzo’s tone of voice</a> guide). This is particularly important for communicating complex issues and priorities to non-experts</li> <li>You're impact driven and eager to have a real positive impact on the company, our products, our users and your team-mates</li> <li>You have a self-starter mindset<em>;</em> you proactively identify issues and opportunities and tackle them without being told to do so</li> <li>You're a team player<em> </em>whom your colleagues can rely on</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🌈 The application journey has 4 key steps</strong></p> <ol> <li>Initial call with a member of the Forecasting team</li> <li>Technical modelling interview </li> <li>Values and collaboration behavioural interview</li> <li>A live case study problem solving interview</li> </ol> <p>Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰 £79,000 to £106,800 + <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">benefits</a>  </p> <p>📍 London (one day a week)</p> <p>✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK</p> <p>✅ We can sponsor visas</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.</p> <p>📚Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences</p> <p>➕And much more, see our full list of benefits <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">here</a></p> <p> </p> <p><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">#LI-JH1</span></p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. to demos and sales;  to ensuring successful account switch and activation.</li> <li>Guiding customers through Monzo’s business banking offerings - providing clear, factual information and helping them evaluate what works best.</li> <li>Being a product expert: fully understand Monzo's business banking products, features and services.</li> <li>Managing a pipeline of leads with strong attention to data hygiene: timely follow-ups, accurate forecasting, deal tracking.</li> <li>Driving activation: not just closing, but ensuring new business customers are fully set up, onboarded, and are using Monzo for their banking needs.</li> <li>Collaborating internally: work closely with marketing, product, risk and customer operations to ensure a smooth journey for customers.</li> <li>Delivering outstanding service at every touchpoint: via phone, video, email or digital channels.</li> <li>Achieving sales targets: conversion, activations, revenue, engagement and other growth metrics as set by the commercial leadership.</li> <li>Feeding insights back: capture and share customer feedback — customer pain points, required features, suggestions for product improvements.</li> <li>Adapting & iterate: Things will change rapidly and often - you’ll need to be comfortable with ambiguity and change and help support what comes next.</li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if you...</strong></p> <ul> <li>Have experience in Small Business sales, ideally selling business solutions or financial services; you simplify complex topics for customers.</li> <li>Are coachable and comfortable seeking constructive criticism to empower continuous learning and improvement</li> <li>Are comfortable working in a fast-moving, high change environment. among the most valued software suppliers to the Global 10,000.</p> <p><strong>Location:</strong> This is a remote role in AMER or EMEA time zones, with the option to be based in our London office.</p> title: Manager, Solutions Consultants, UKI
description: WHO WE ARE Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: The Solutions Consultant Manager is the person who makes our GTM motion real on the ground. As an in-region leader directly managing a team of Solutions Consultants, you'll own your team's full commercial output—new logo, expansion, and renewals—and be accountable for both the results and the quality of execution that produces them. This isn't a traditional pipeline-management role. The best SC Managers are coaches first: they know what a great first meeting looks like, can watch a live build and tell a rep exactly what to change, and build the operating rhythm and inspection cadence that makes consistent execution possible across the team. If you're a builder who loves developing people as much as winning deals—and you want to lead a regional team in a go-to-market model that's genuinely new—this is the role. This role will be based in London, UK. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Own the commercial performance of your team across new logo ARR, expansion ARR, and UBP outcomes—accountable for both the headline numbers and the quality of execution that drives them - Coach SCs on the GTM builder motion: what great looks like in a first meeting (workflow diagnosis, current → future architecture), a second meeting (live build in Notion + value narrative), and through the full cycle to adoption hand-off - Contribute to and participate in the regional operating cadence: weekly pipeline reviews, deal support sessions, call reviews against the motion quality rubric, and forecast calls with senior leadership - Hire, onboard, and certify new SCs to the GTM builder motion—driving readiness from ramp through consistent execution, and managing performance with clarity when expectations aren't met - Partner with the regional BDR manager on pipeline strategy, outbound targeting, and qualification standards to ensure the team's book of business is healthy and growing - Partner with Outcomes leadership on adoption hand-offs, at-risk account management, and renewal strategy—owning the overall commercial arc for the region while collaborating on the execution that follows close - Represent your team or region in leadership forums with clear signal on what's working, what needs investment, and where execution is breaking down SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: - Track record as a quota-carrying B2B seller with direct experience in workflow design, live demos, or technical sales—you can coach the builder motion because you've run it yourself - Frontline sales management experience: built an operating cadence, ran performance management, and developed talent from onboarding through consistent overperformance - Strong coaching orientation: you can watch a demo or deal review and identify specifically what to change—not just whether the outcome was good, but why, and what the rep should do differently next time - description: <p>We are hiring a <strong>Global Payroll Manager</strong>, ideally a candidate who thrives on building scalable systems, automating manual processes, and creating operational excellence in a high growth technology environment. </p> <p>We are looking for a leader who combines deep payroll expertise with a systems oriented mindset. professionals</li> <li>Ensure compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements while identifying and managing compliance risks.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What we are looking for in you will match our values, by being:</p> <ul> <li>Precise, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity</li> <li>Reliable, delivering high quality work that builds trust and confidence</li> <li>Accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable</li> <li>Adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Nice-to-have skills</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience implementing or optimizing payroll platforms and HRIS systems</li> <li>Payroll management experience in publicly traded or pre-IPO companies</li> <li>A passion for technology and a desire to work with motivated colleagues</li> <li>Experience supporting rapid expansion, including new country payroll launches</li> <li>A passion for technology and a desire to work with motivated colleagues</li> <li>MBA or other relevant business degree</li> </ul> <h3>What we offer colleagues</h3> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping This role is open to candidates based in North America and the United Kingdom. You can work from anywhere within these regions.
